Q: Late binding in Racket Scheme can't be found in a let-environment A:

Scheme is a statically scoped language, which means that the binding of a variable is determined by the nearest enclosing define or let in the source code.

In your version that works, later-func is defined in the outermost scope, so can be seen from inside of outer. But in the version that doesn't, you'd have to look inside of the let to find the definition of later-func from inside of the definition of outer; it doesn't matter that you are calling outer from inside that let.

Q: Python RE didn't find the last empty string in back reference pattern A:

Seems the behavior might be different for different engines.
A good search string would be :
can regex match a backreference to a group that exists but is undefined.

The way backreferernces work for Perl, PCRE and Python engines is like this ->

When it comes to backreferences the engines discards undefined capture groups.
This is tested using an empty string target for clarity.
The empty string target will boil it down to it's essence behavior.
Adding characters will in no way changes the behavior, but it might make it
harder to understand.

Demonstrated using an empty string target >>>>

Capture 1 contains empty string -> 1 match (1?)\1
PCRE https://regex101.com/r/eLCc0b/1
Python https://regex101.com/r/0d8pnS/1

vs

Capture 1 is undefined -> 0 match (1)?\1
PCRE https://regex101.com/r/SSW2Fc/1
Python https://regex101.com/r/oy5k3t/1

This is actually a fairly important distinction. Any group that didn't match it's contents is undefined.

Doesn't matter what the quantifier is outside the group.
Capture 1 is undefined -> 0 match (1){0}\1
PCRE https://regex101.com/r/cAAcc6/1 Python https://regex101.com/r/gmX92V/1

Finally, using a backreference to an undefined capture group will fail the match
at that point unless there is an alternate path of course.
This should be tested upon all flavor engines though.

Q: How should an OIDC client application determine if a user can access UI components? A:

Put sensitive elements in a separate page and call the backend to determine whether or not to show links and the page itself. I just think doing individual element control is way too messy. Also, you cannot control access by attempting to not show FE elements because you also have to block access to the BE APIs. Get a book.
